decisions.reason: As a core printer technology close to the firm's established marking systems and backed by strong in-house R&D, this product fits the firm's knowledge base and is likely to be improved rather than withdrawn.

This software module extends the existing coding portfolio in a direction consistent with digitalization and variable-data printing, so the firm has the absorptive capacity to learn from and retain it.
An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces builds directly on the firm's established inkjet and substrate expertise, making continued commercialization more likely than exit.

Although somewhat more peripheral than the firm's hardware core, the app is still close to its decoding and traceability capabilities and even builds on a predecessor, so it is more likely to be kept than dropped.
An inline code verification system strongly matches the firm's move toward serialization and end-to-end traceability, and its existing technical and service capabilities support further development.
Print layout design software complements the firm's installed base and common-operation strategy, so a large R&D-performing firm in this field would usually keep it on the market.
